text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele said that the model and principles of the new government will be made known to political parties next Tuesday.
- Leaders of Latvia's Way and Fatherland & Freedom factions have signed an agreement about the basic principles of forming the government.
- The law on compulsory motor insurance was passed by the parliament, to come into force as of August 1 1997.
- IGE TV was granted a licence to broadcast on channel two of Latvian TV.
- Baltic leaders have been invited to participate in the inauguration ceremony of newly-elected president of Chechnya, Aslan Maskhadov.
- The Latvian and Estonian welfare ministers signed an agreement on the application of a treaty on co-operation in the social sphere.
- Lithuania invited Latvia to start a constructive and effective dialogue on the sea border issue. The proposed date to start talks in Vilnius is February 4.
- A favourable credit rating and the quick resolution of the government crisis made one-year Treasury bill rates plummet to 8.21 percent on January 29 from 12.37 percent.
- The Latvian Privatization Agency has launched an Internet home page to provide information on companies available for privatisation in Latvia. The site is found at WWW.LPA.BKC.LV.
- The Latvian-based branch of the Norwegian investment company, Varner Hakon Invest, won the tender to re-construct Riga railway station for mote than $6 million.
